patterns.name: INDEPENDENT COGNITIVE ARCHITECTURES
patterns.interpretation: Multiple AGI approaches (symbolic, connectionist, hybrid) co-exist as independent research programs, each with its own knowledge representation.

patterns.name: THE DISTRIBUTION OF COGNITIVE SUBSYSTEMS
patterns.interpretation: Cognitive subsystems (perception, reasoning, learning, action) distribute across the architecture following natural information-flow boundaries.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE ECOSYSTEM FINGERS
patterns.interpretation: Symbolic and sub-symbolic processing interleave like fingers â€” neither dominates; they interpenetrate at every scale.

patterns.name: LEARNING VALLEYS
patterns.interpretation: Deep specialization channels where intensive learning occurs â€” MOSES evolving programs, PLN refining beliefs, miner discovering patterns.

patterns.name: LACE OF INFERENCE PATHS
patterns.interpretation: Inference chains form a lace-like network â€” no single path dominates; multiple reasoning routes reach the same conclusion with different confidence.

patterns.name: SATELLITE COGNITIVE MODULES
patterns.interpretation: Peripheral cognitive modules (vision, motor, NLP) orbit the central AtomSpace, connecting when needed but maintaining autonomy.

patterns.name: THE OPEN COGNITIVE ECOSYSTEM
patterns.interpretation: The broader landscape of cognitive science tools, frameworks, and theories from which OpenCog draws and to which it contributes.

patterns.name: MOSAIC OF REPRESENTATIONS
patterns.interpretation: Multiple knowledge representations coexist: Atomese, Link Grammar, probabilistic weights, attention values â€” each suited to different cognitive tasks.

patterns.name: DISTRIBUTED COGNITION
patterns.interpretation: Cognitive processing distributes across networked AtomSpaces â€” no single node holds all knowledge; federation enables scale.

patterns.name: MAGIC OF THE HYPERGRAPH
patterns.interpretation: The AtomSpace hypergraph enables emergent cognitive phenomena that no single subsystem could produce â€” the whole exceeds the sum.

patterns.name: LOCAL INFERENCE AREAS
patterns.interpretation: Inference bounded to local subgraphs â€” reasoning scoped to relevant context rather than the entire knowledge base.

patterns.name: COMMUNITY OF COGNITIVE AGENTS
patterns.interpretation: Multiple cognitive agents cohabit the AtomSpace, each specializing in different tasks while sharing the common knowledge substrate.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE BOUNDARY
patterns.interpretation: Clear boundaries between cognitive subsystems â€” perception doesn't directly write motor commands; information flows through defined interfaces.

patterns.name: IDENTIFIABLE COGNITIVE MODULE
patterns.interpretation: Each cognitive module has a clear identity, purpose, and interface â€” you can point to 'the reasoner' or 'the pattern miner' as distinct entities.

patterns.name: MODULE SCOPE BOUNDARY
patterns.interpretation: Each module's scope is explicitly bounded â€” PLN reasons over probabilistic logic, not motor control; ECAN allocates attention, not memory.

patterns.name: WEB OF PUBLIC ATOM TYPES
patterns.interpretation: The shared Atom type hierarchy forms a public API â€” any module can create/read Atoms of public types, enabling interoperability.

patterns.name: RING OF COGNITIVE FEEDBACK
patterns.interpretation: Perception-cognition-action loops form rings â€” sensory input drives reasoning, reasoning drives action, action changes perception.

patterns.name: NETWORK OF LEARNING
patterns.interpretation: Learning subsystems form a network â€” MOSES learns programs, PLN learns beliefs, the miner learns patterns, each feeding the others.

patterns.name: WEB OF KNOWLEDGE STORES
patterns.interpretation: Multiple storage backends (RocksDB, PostgreSQL, CogServer network) form a web of persistent knowledge accessible to all subsystems.

patterns.name: MICRO-AGENTS
patterns.interpretation: Small, focused cognitive agents that handle one task â€” a link-type checker, a truth-value updater, an attention redistributor.

patterns.name: FOUR-LAYER COGNITIVE LIMIT
patterns.interpretation: Cognitive processing should not exceed ~4 levels of abstraction in a single inference step â€” deeper reasoning must be chunked.

patterns.name: NINE PERCENT METACOGNITION
patterns.interpretation: ~9% of cognitive resources should go to metacognition (monitoring, attention allocation) â€” too little loses coherence, too much wastes capacity.

patterns.name: PARALLEL INFERENCE PIPELINES
patterns.interpretation: Multiple inference chains execute in parallel â€” forward chaining, backward chaining, and pattern matching run concurrently on shared AtomSpace.

patterns.name: SACRED KNOWLEDGE STRUCTURES
patterns.interpretation: Core ontological structures (type hierarchy, fundamental inference rules) that must not be corrupted â€” they are the bedrock of all reasoning.

patterns.name: ACCESS TO EXPERIENCE
patterns.interpretation: Every cognitive module must have access to the experiential stream â€” raw percepts, grounded symbols, embodied knowledge.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE LIFE CYCLE
patterns.interpretation: Knowledge has a life cycle: acquisition â†’ integration â†’ consolidation â†’ retrieval â†’ revision â†’ forgetting. Systems must support all phases.

patterns.name: SYMBOLIC AND SUBSYMBOLIC
patterns.interpretation: The symbolic layer (Atomese, logic) faces the reasoning; the subsymbolic layer (embeddings, attention values) provides the grounding.

patterns.name: ATTENTION GATEWAY
patterns.interpretation: ECAN acts as the gateway â€” controlling which Atoms get processing resources, routing attention to relevant subgraphs.

patterns.name: DEPENDENCY RINGS OF COGNITION
patterns.interpretation: Circular dependencies in cognition are natural: perception needs concepts, concepts need perception. Managed through iterative refinement.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE ACTIVITY NODES

patterns.name: COGNITIVE PORTAL

patterns.name: KNOWLEDGE MARKETPLACE

patterns.name: BACKGROUND COGNITION

patterns.name: COGNITIVE MESSAGE PASSING
patterns.interpretation: Inter-module communication via Atoms â€” modules write structured messages into the AtomSpace rather than calling each other directly.

patterns.name: REPRESENTATION MIX

patterns.name: DEGREES OF COGNITIVE ACCESS

patterns.name: KNOWLEDGE CLUSTER

patterns.name: MONOLITHIC KNOWLEDGE BASE

patterns.name: LEGACY KNOWLEDGE EVERYWHERE

patterns.name: COGNITIVE COMMUNITY

patterns.name: INFERENCE PIPELINE

patterns.name: COGNITIVE SCIENCE MARKETPLACE

patterns.name: NETWORK OF INFERENCE PATHS

patterns.name: EXPERT AND NOVICE KNOWLEDGE

patterns.name: KNOWLEDGE BASE COMPLEX

patterns.name: NUMBER OF ABSTRACTION LAYERS

patterns.name: COGNITIVE ONBOARDING FLOW

patterns.interpretation: The mechanism for reviewing proposed beliefs - checking consistency, evaluating evidence, comparing with existing knowledge.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE TEST DATA
patterns.interpretation: Curated data sets for testing cognitive capabilities - known-answer inference problems, benchmark tasks.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE GARBAGE COLLECTION
patterns.interpretation: Removing irrelevant, decayed, or contradicted knowledge - attention-driven forgetting for manageability.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE HELPER FUNCTIONS
patterns.interpretation: Small cognitive utilities - truth value calculators, confidence mergers, link traversal helpers.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE INSPECTION POINT
patterns.interpretation: Points where cognitive processing can be observed - breakpoints in inference chains, attention monitors.

patterns.name: THE INFERENCE PROCESS
patterns.interpretation: The structured process by which conclusions are built - rule selection, unification, truth value computation, commitment.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE ATMOSPHERE
patterns.interpretation: The ambient cognitive state - overall attention levels, default reasoning strategies, background processing load.

patterns.name: ISOLATED COGNITIVE CONTEXT
patterns.interpretation: Reasoning within an isolated context - hypothetical worlds, counterfactual scenarios, sandboxed inference.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE CONFIGURATION
patterns.interpretation: Configuration of cognitive parameters - attention decay rates, inference depth limits, confidence thresholds.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE SYNCHRONIZATION
patterns.interpretation: Periodic synchronization between cognitive subsystems - aligning goals, sharing discoveries, coordinating attention.

patterns.name: SHARED COGNITIVE STATE
patterns.interpretation: State shared across cognitive modules via the AtomSpace - the global blackboard where all subsystems read and write.

patterns.name: CORE COGNITIVE INTEGRATION
patterns.interpretation: The integration point where all cognitive subsystems converge - the AtomSpace as universal meeting ground.

patterns.name: PRIVATE COGNITIVE SCOPE
patterns.interpretation: Module-private knowledge not visible to other subsystems - internal heuristics, working hypotheses.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE PREPROCESSING
patterns.interpretation: Initial processing of raw input - tokenization, feature extraction, normalization, grounding.

patterns.name: ABSTRACTION LEVEL VARIETY
patterns.interpretation: Knowledge at multiple abstraction levels coexisting - raw percepts alongside high-level theories.

patterns.name: THE SHAPE OF KNOWLEDGE SPACE
patterns.interpretation: The topological structure of the knowledge graph - clusters, bridges, peripheries, cores.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE MONITORING DASHBOARDS
patterns.interpretation: Real-time displays of cognitive system health - inference throughput, attention distribution, memory pressure.

patterns.name: SEMI-PUBLIC COGNITIVE API
patterns.interpretation: Cognitive interfaces available to trusted modules but not externally - internal service APIs.

patterns.name: INTERNAL COGNITIVE INTERFACES
patterns.interpretation: Internal interfaces between cognitive subsystems - how pattern matcher talks to URE, how ECAN talks to AtomSpace.

patterns.name: INFERENCE DEPTH
patterns.interpretation: The depth of nested inference - how many reasoning steps deep before stopping and returning partial results.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE ESCAPE HATCHES
patterns.interpretation: Emergency mechanisms for escaping infinite inference loops, attention traps, or deadlocked reasoning.

patterns.name: ROBUST COGNITIVE BOUNDARIES
patterns.interpretation: Strong boundaries preventing cognitive contamination - one modules errors dont propagate unchecked.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE ADAPTERS
patterns.interpretation: Adapter layers translating between different cognitive representations - Atomese to vectors, logic to probability.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE METRICS DASHBOARD
patterns.interpretation: Quantitative cognitive metrics - inference accuracy, attention efficiency, learning rate, knowledge growth.

patterns.name: EXPOSED COGNITIVE CONFIGURATION
patterns.interpretation: Cognitive parameters tunable externally - inference depth, attention decay, confidence thresholds.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE MIDDLEWARE
patterns.interpretation: Processing layers between raw input and cognitive engagement - filtering, routing, prioritizing.

patterns.name: BUILT-IN COGNITIVE UTILITIES
patterns.interpretation: Core utilities built into the AtomSpace - type checking, truth value operations, basic pattern matching.

patterns.name: NESTED COGNITIVE SCOPES
patterns.interpretation: Hierarchically nested reasoning contexts - global beliefs containing domain beliefs containing task hypotheses.

patterns.name: HIDDEN COGNITIVE FEATURES
patterns.interpretation: Latent cognitive capabilities not yet activated - dormant inference rules, unused Atom types.

patterns.name: STRUCTURE FOLLOWS COGNITIVE SPACES
patterns.interpretation: The code architecture mirrors the cognitive architecture - each component directory maps to a cognitive subsystem.

patterns.name: EFFICIENT KNOWLEDGE BASE
patterns.interpretation: A knowledge base optimized for the operations most frequently performed - fast pattern matching, efficient attention lookup.

patterns.name: GOOD COGNITIVE DEPENDENCIES
patterns.interpretation: Clean dependency relationships between cognitive modules - no circular imports, clear layering, validated DAG.

patterns.name: GRADUAL COGNITIVE FORMALIZATION
patterns.interpretation: Knowledge starts informal (natural language, fuzzy concepts) and gradually formalizes into precise Atomese as understanding deepens.

patterns.name: KNOWLEDGE BASE LAYOUT
patterns.interpretation: The structural layout of the knowledge base - how Atoms are organized, indexed, and made navigable.

patterns.name: ATOM TYPE STRUCTURE
patterns.interpretation: The organization of Atom types into coherent packages - Node types, Link types, Value types, each with clear semantics.

patterns.name: HARDENING THE COGNITIVE API
patterns.interpretation: Making cognitive interfaces robust - input validation, error handling, graceful degradation under load.

patterns.name: CORE COGNITIVE MODULES
patterns.interpretation: The irreducible core modules: atomspace (storage), cogutil (utilities), unify (matching), ure (inference).

patterns.name: FINAL MODULE DISTRIBUTION
patterns.interpretation: The settled distribution of cognitive responsibilities across modules after architecture has matured.

patterns.name: BASE ATOM CLASSES
patterns.interpretation: The foundational Atom class hierarchy - Atom > Node/Link > specific types - from which all knowledge structures derive.

patterns.name: FOUNDATION COGNITIVE LAYER
patterns.interpretation: The foundational layer (Tier 0) - cogutil and atomspace - upon which everything else is built.

patterns.name: CONTAINER ATOMS
patterns.interpretation: Atoms that contain other Atoms - SetLink, ListLink, AndLink - providing structure and grouping.

patterns.name: BOUNDARY VALIDATORS
patterns.interpretation: Validation at cognitive boundaries - type checking Atoms before insertion, confidence checking before commitment.

patterns.name: INTERFACE CONTRACTS
patterns.interpretation: Formal contracts between cognitive modules - expected Atom types, required truth value ranges, guaranteed response times.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE ABSTRACTION LAYERS
patterns.interpretation: The layered abstraction of the cognitive architecture - atoms > patterns > rules > strategies > meta-strategies.

patterns.name: TOP-LEVEL COGNITIVE EXPORTS
patterns.interpretation: The top-level capabilities exported by the cognitive system - what external systems can invoke and rely upon.

patterns.name: NATURAL COGNITIVE ENTRY POINTS
patterns.interpretation: Intuitive ways to interact with the system - natural language input, visual queries, gestural commands.

patterns.name: LOW BARRIER TO COGNITION
patterns.interpretation: Making cognitive capabilities accessible without deep expertise - simple APIs, clear defaults, helpful error messages.

patterns.name: DETAILED COGNITIVE DOCUMENTATION
patterns.interpretation: Thorough documentation of cognitive mechanisms - how inference works, how attention flows, how learning occurs.

patterns.name: MINIMAL COGNITIVE INTERFACE
patterns.interpretation: The smallest possible interface to a cognitive capability - do one thing well, expose minimum necessary state.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE CONTRACTS
patterns.interpretation: Module interfaces as formal contracts - if you provide Atoms of type X, I guarantee conclusions of type Y with confidence Z.

patterns.name: SINGLETON COGNITIVE PATTERNS
patterns.interpretation: One-of-a-kind cognitive structures - the single attention focus, the single goal stack, the single active context.

patterns.name: MODULE COGNITIVE DEPENDENCIES
patterns.interpretation: The explicit dependency graph between cognitive modules - atomspace depends on cogutil, ure depends on unify.

patterns.name: RECURSIVE COGNITIVE CALLS
patterns.interpretation: Self-referential cognitive operations - meta-reasoning about reasoning, learning to learn, attention to attention.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE LOGGING
patterns.interpretation: Comprehensive logging of cognitive events - inference steps taken, attention shifts, beliefs modified, goals pursued.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE EVENT PROPAGATION
patterns.interpretation: How cognitive events propagate through the system - attention changes rippling through connected Atoms.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE DEBUG ENDPOINTS
patterns.interpretation: Interfaces for debugging cognitive processing - step-through inference, attention inspection, belief querying.

patterns.name: KNOWLEDGE VERSION TAGS
patterns.interpretation: Tags marking significant states of the knowledge base - before/after learning, pre/post revision, checkpoint states.

patterns.name: BASE COGNITIVE TYPES
patterns.interpretation: The primitive types from which all cognitive structures are built - Node, Link, TruthValue, AttentionValue.

patterns.name: PUBLIC COGNITIVE API
patterns.interpretation: The stable, versioned public API for external cognitive system interaction.

patterns.name: INTERNAL COGNITIVE API
patterns.interpretation: Internal APIs between cognitive subsystems - not guaranteed stable, optimized for performance over usability.

patterns.name: EXTENSIBLE COGNITIVE INTERFACES
patterns.interpretation: Interfaces designed for extension - new Atom types can be added, new inference rules registered, new attention policies plugged in.

patterns.name: TYPED COGNITIVE INTERFACES
patterns.interpretation: Strongly typed cognitive interfaces - Atom type system enforces correct usage, prevents meaningless combinations.

patterns.name: SANITIZED COGNITIVE INPUT
patterns.interpretation: Input validation for cognitive processing - malformed Atoms rejected, out-of-range truth values clamped, circular links detected.

patterns.name: SMALL COGNITIVE FUNCTIONS
patterns.interpretation: Small, composable cognitive primitives - individual inference steps, atomic attention updates, single pattern matches.

patterns.name: CONSISTENT COGNITIVE FORMATTING
patterns.interpretation: Consistent representation of knowledge - uniform Atom naming, standardized truth value scales, regular link structures.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE BREAKPOINTS
patterns.interpretation: Points where cognitive processing can be paused for inspection - inference step boundaries, attention cycle ends.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE WELCOME MESSAGE
patterns.interpretation: The initial greeting when interacting with the cognitive system - current state summary, available commands, active goals.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE GUARD CLAUSES
patterns.interpretation: Early termination conditions in cognitive processing - if preconditions not met, abort inference immediately.

patterns.name: TEMPORARY COGNITIVE SOLUTIONS
patterns.interpretation: Provisional knowledge marked as temporary - placeholders until better information arrives, heuristics pending formal proof.

patterns.name: HIGHLIGHTED COGNITIVE FEATURES
patterns.interpretation: Attention-highlighted knowledge structures - Atoms with high STI that are currently salient and actively being processed.

patterns.name: PROGRESSIVE COGNITIVE ENHANCEMENT
patterns.interpretation: Cognitive capabilities that degrade gracefully - if full inference is too slow, fall back to cached results or heuristics.

patterns.name: GRACEFUL COGNITIVE DEGRADATION
patterns.interpretation: The system remains functional under resource pressure - reduced inference depth, narrower attention, approximate reasoning.

patterns.name: FLEXIBLE COGNITIVE TYPES
patterns.interpretation: Type system flexibility - Atoms can participate in multiple type hierarchies, types can be refined incrementally.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE DOCUMENTATION
patterns.interpretation: Self-documentation of the cognitive system - every module describes its purpose, capabilities, and interfaces.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE IDENTITY
patterns.interpretation: The cognitive systems sense of self - its own identity, capabilities, limitations, and purpose as represented in its knowledge.

patterns.name: DIVERSE COGNITIVE TOOLS
patterns.interpretation: The variety of cognitive tools available - different reasoners, different learners, different matchers for different tasks.

patterns.name: COGNITIVE ANNOTATIONS
patterns.interpretation: Annotations on knowledge structures - why a belief is held, when it was acquired, what evidence supports it, how confident we are.

patterns.name: PERSONAL COGNITIVE TOUCHES
patterns.interpretation: Individual personality in the cognitive system - unique reasoning styles, preferred heuristics, characteristic attention patterns that make each instance distinct.
